safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states NKDA, but Generated only says allergies were discussed without documenting 'no known drug allergies'.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document NKDA leaves allergy status ambiguous, which can increase the risk of inappropriate prescribing or delays if future clinicians assume allergies are unknown and must be re-verified before treatment. While no specific high-risk drug was started here, allergy documentation is clinically important for safe medication management.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Neither Gold nor transcript states an instruction to continue metformin as part of the visit plan.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Adding an unsubstantiated plan item (“continue metformin”) can create documentation noise and could confuse the patient or downstream clinicians about what was explicitly reviewed or advised during this visit. In this case it is unlikely to cause harm because the patient is already taking metformin and no change was discussed.
